extra.message: The `host` query parameter of GET /ops/shell/ticket-probe-505 is concatenated directly into a shell command executed via os.system(). Any attacker able to reach the endpoint can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id) and achieve arbitrary OS command execution as the application user.

extra.message: The `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template source string and then rendered. Jinja2 templates are compiled to Python, so a payload such as fragment={{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen('id').read() }} yields server-side template injection and arbitrary code execution. The rendered result is also returned as HTML, enabling XSS.

extra.message: The `packet_ref` query parameter of POST /ops/dock/ticket-spool-slot-058 is joined onto the export directory with no canonicalisation, confinement check, or allowlist, and the raw request body is written to the resulting path. A value like `../../../../home/app/.ssh/authorized_keys` (or `/etc/cron.d/x`, since Path joining with an absolute string discards the base) lets an attacker write arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, leading to remote code execution.

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-500 builds the destination path by joining the attacker-supplied `name` query parameter to BASE_EXPORT_DIR and writes the request body there, including creating parent directories. extra.message: POST /ops/mongo/ticket-lane-545 takes the JSON request body (or its `filter` key) and passes it verbatim as the MongoDB query document to find_one(). An attacker fully controls the query operators, so payloads such as {"filter": {"$where": "..."}} or {"filter": {"secret": {"$ne": null}}} allow authentication-style bypass, arbitrary record enumeration, and server-side JavaScript evaluation.

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/ticket-gate-525 derives the privilege decision from the `ops_badge` cookie or the `x-ops-badge` request header. Both are fully attacker-controlled, so simply sending `x-ops-badge: lead` returns the elevated response containing payroll and casework data. Authorization must be derived from authoritative server-side session/identity state, not client-supplied values.

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/ticket-rebind-196 builds a server-side workset containing security-relevant fields (`role`, `tier`, `approved`, `balance`) and then merges the unvalidated JSON request body over it with dict.update(). A client can therefore assert its own role/approval/balance (e.g. {"role":"admin","approved":true}) and the elevated values are accepted and returned as the effective workset.

extra.message: GET /ops/after/ticket-lane-153 passes the caller-supplied `lane` query parameter straight into RedirectResponse with no allowlist or same-origin validation. extra.message: POST /ops/digest/ticket-fold-276 hashes the supplied `phrase` with hashlib.md5(). MD5 is collision-broken and, being fast and unsalted, is trivially reversible for passphrase-sized inputs via rainbow tables. It must not be used to digest secrets or for any integrity purpose.

extra.message: GET /ops/spool/ticket-fan-311 builds a list of `count` dictionaries where `count` is an unbounded caller-supplied integer with no maximum. extra.message: POST /api/auth/login performs an unlimited number of password verifications: there is no per-account lockout, no failed-attempt counter, no delay, and no rate-limiting middleware anywhere in the request path (the only middleware registered on the app is CORSMiddleware at main.py:70). An attacker can brute-force credentials for any known account, including the seeded admin, at full request rate. The same absence applies to the registration and password-reset endpoints.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The login handler raises 401 on unknown email, inactive account, or wrong password and returns immediately, so no AuditLog record is written; the audit() call only runs on the success path (main.py:168). Authorization failures raised by require_role/ensure_ticket_access in authz.py are likewise never recorded, and no middleware or exception handler supplies logging. Credential-stuffing and privilege-probing campaigns therefore leave no durable security audit trail, defeating detection and forensics.

extra.message: The session cookie is set with secure=False, so the browser transmits the `support_session` bearer token over plaintext HTTP. Combined with samesite="lax" and a 12-hour lifetime, any network attacker able to observe or trigger an HTTP request to the host can capture a valid session token and fully impersonate the user. The flag is hardcoded rather than driven by configuration.
